50 UGC Product Ideas You Already Own (2026 Checklist)

This is a free, updated checklist of 50 everyday products you can film for a UGC portfolio even if no brand has sent you a box. Each row has what to shoot, the shots to get, and a first line you can say in the opening three seconds. You can film in your bathroom, kitchen, or at your desk with things you already have.

Last updated: August 2026. We keep this list current. Film 8 to 12 of these and you have enough samples to start pitching.

Already have samples and want paid work? See our list of brands that pay for UGC. Want gifted product instead? Use the companies that send PR packages directory.

Get These Clips in Front of Brands

Brands look at sample videos before they look at follower counts. Add yours to a free newcollab profile so brands hiring UGC creators can send offers directly.

What to Film First

Start with eight products most people already have: cleanser, moisturizer, SPF, wireless earbuds, a coffee mug, a tote bag, protein powder or vitamins, and shampoo. That mix hits the categories brands buy most. Keep each video 15-30 seconds, vertical (9:16), on your phone, with the product readable on screen.

  • PR is not required. Sample videos of products you bought yourself are how a lot of UGC creators land their first paid brief.
  • Follower count does not matter here. Brands are buying the clip. See the difference in our UGC vs influencer marketing guide.
  • A window is enough. A cheap tripod helps more than a fancy camera.

How to use this UGC checklist

Work through one category at a time so you do not stall:

  1. Walk around your place and tick every product below that you already own.
  2. Pick two from each category so the folder is not only skincare.
  3. Follow the What to film column. That is what most brand briefs ask for.
  4. Use the hook or write your own first line. Brands decide in the first three seconds whether to keep watching.
  5. Export 9:16 with captions. Skip music you do not have rights to, or use the app's commercial library.
  6. Upload 8 to 12 clips to Google Drive and your newcollab profile.

For production tips (lighting, hooks, CTAs), see how to create high-impact UGC for brands.

How to Film a UGC Sample Video

Use the same setup for every product. After a few takes, each clip takes about 10 minutes.

1. Setup

  • Face a window. Turn off overhead lights if they mix with daylight.
  • Put the phone on a tripod, or lean it on a mug at eye level. Avoid shooting the whole thing handheld.
  • Wipe the product and the surface so the label is readable.
  • Record in 9:16. Tap the screen to lock exposure.

2. Shoot four short clips

  1. Hook (3 seconds): talking to camera, start with the problem.
  2. Product insert (2-4 seconds): label, texture, unbox, or pour.
  3. Use (8-15 seconds): apply, wear, eat, or press play.
  4. Close (3-5 seconds): a simple wrap like "this is staying in my kit."

3. Edit

  • Cut the dead air. Add captions. Skip a long intro.
  • Keep it 15-30 seconds. Brands trim longer files anyway.
  • Leave the watermark off. Brands cannot run ads with your handle burned in.
  • Export 1080x1920 and name the file something clear, like cleanser-ugc.mp4.

What Brands Look For in a UGC Portfolio

Before you pitch, check these:

  • Readable product: logo or label in frame for at least one second.
  • Your voice on the track: skip trending sounds you cannot license.
  • One idea per video: "this serum under makeup" works better than a full routine.
  • More than one category: beauty plus home, tech, or food books more briefs.
  • It sounds like you: if it reads like a script, film it again.

Need a one-pager to send with the Drive folder? Use this 30-minute media kit template.

FAQ

Do I need brands to send me products before I can make UGC?

No. Sample videos of products you already own are how most UGC creators get hired. Film the checklist, then pitch brands in the same category. Paid briefs usually include a shipped product after you are booked.

How many UGC sample videos do I need in my portfolio?

Eight is enough to start pitching. Twelve is better. Three clean 20-second clips beat a folder of 20 messy ones. Cover at least two categories, for example skincare and home.

Can I film drugstore and supermarket products?

Yes. Brands want to see your filming style, lighting, and voice. A $6 cleanser video can win a $150 serum brief if the hook and texture shots are clean.

What format do brands want for UGC samples?

Vertical 9:16, 15-30 seconds, captions on, no watermark, 1080p. Deliver MP4. Keep samples in Drive or on your newcollab profile rather than posting every spec on your public grid.

Is it legal to film products I bought myself?

Yes for your portfolio and for pitching. Do not imply the brand hired you, and do not use their trademarked slogans as if you are an official ad. When a brand pays you, they will send usage terms.

What should I do after I film these 50 ideas?

Pick your best 8 to 12. Upload them to a Drive folder and a newcollab creator profile. Then pitch brands that pay for UGC in those categories, or wait for inbound offers. Getting the samples in front of a buyer matters more than filming all 50.
